newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar slips off highs, trade supports.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar slips off highs, trade supports.

text.p: White sugar futures backed off earlier higher as the raws market failed to correct higher but London's low prices sparked supportive offtake, traders said on Wednesday.
Outright trade purchases mainly accounted for the steadiness of the two nearby contracts during the afternoon although commission houses were active buyers earlier, they said.
"There's nothing out of the ordinary and it's all trade buying," said one trader, noting flat price purchases on both nearby positions.
"There is offtake around, especially at these levels which are slightly more attractive," he said, citing demand in Iran, Indonesia and Pakistan.
At 1714 GMT March was up 30 cents at $294.40 after firming to an intraday high of $297.00. May was up $1.20 at $295.50.
Volume totalled a hefty 3,183 lots, boosted by limited crosses and dealings on the March/May spread.
In Colombia, talks aimed at ending a week-old dockworkers' strike in the Pacific port of Buenaventura ended in a deadlock early on Wednesday.
Buenaventura is the shipping point for all of Colombia's sugar exports and is estimated to be losing $500,000 for every day it remains closed.
Paris positions were all slightly firmer in an overall volume of 1,092 lots.
March was up 80 cents at $294.50 and May was up by the same amount at $295.50.
